blurb.en: Read notes, signs and messages carefully, then choose the line that fits a conversation.
blurb.vi: Đọc kĩ ghi chú, biển báo và tin nhắn, rồi chọn câu thoại phù hợp trong hội thoại.

must.def: It is a rule, so you have no choice about doing it.
must.ex: Players *must* wear a helmet on the bike track.

mustn't.def: It is not allowed. Do not do it.
mustn't.ex: You *mustn't* run near the swimming pool.

need to.def: It is necessary. Without it, you can't do the activity.
need to.ex: You *need to* bring a hat for the school trip.

don't have to.def: It is not necessary, but you can do it if you like.
don't have to.ex: You *don't have to* bring water: there is a free tap in the hall.

should.def: It is a good idea. We use it to give advice.
should.ex: You *should* drink lots of water when you have a fever.

notice.def: A short text on a wall or board that gives people information.
notice.ex: The *notice* says the canteen is closed today.

until.def: Up to a certain time, and then it stops.
until.ex: The playground is open *until* five o'clock.

only.def: This one and no other; not more than this.
only.ex: The quiet room is for Grade 4 students *only*.

cancelled.def: If an event is stopped like this, it will not happen.
cancelled.ex: The football match is *cancelled* because of the heavy rain.

reminder.def: A message that helps you remember something you need to do.
reminder.ex: Mum stuck a *reminder* on the fridge: 'Buy eggs!'

reply.def: What you say or write back when someone speaks or writes to you.
reply.ex: Zoe sent a quick *reply*: 'Yes, see you there!'

suggest.def: To give an idea for other people to think about.
suggest.ex: I *suggest* we meet at the park gate.

polite.def: Kind and careful when you speak, for example saying please and thank you.
polite.ex: 'Could you help me, please?' is a *polite* question.

paraphrase.def: To say the same meaning with different words.

title.vi: Từ chỉ quy định trên thông báo

scenes.head: A notice by the school playground
scenes.html:
PLAYGROUND RULES
You *must* wear a hat at break time: the sun is very hot.
You *mustn't* climb on the fence.
You *don't have to* bring a ball: there are balls in the red box.
The big slide is for Grades 4 and 5 *only*.
The playground is open *until* 4.30 p.m.

steps.en: The words in gold tell you the rule. *must* and *need to* mean it is necessary.
steps.vi: Các từ màu vàng cho em biết quy định. *must* và *need to* nghĩa là bắt buộc, cần thiết.

steps.en: *mustn't* means it is not allowed. *don't have to* means it is not necessary: you can bring a ball, but you don't need one.
steps.vi: *mustn't* nghĩa là không được phép. *don't have to* nghĩa là không cần thiết: em có thể mang bóng, nhưng không cần.

steps.en: Small words like *only* and *until* change the meaning a lot. Read them twice!
steps.vi: Những từ nhỏ như *only* và *until* làm thay đổi nghĩa rất nhiều. Hãy đọc chúng hai lần!

title.vi: Ai viết, và viết để làm gì?

scenes.head: A sticky note on the fridge
scenes.html: Iris, I'm at Grandma's house. She *has a bad cough*, so I'm *taking her some soup*. *Please feed the cat at six.* I'll be home by eight. Love, Mum

steps.en: Ask three questions: Who wrote it? Why? What do they want? Mum tells Iris where she is and asks for help.
steps.vi: Hãy hỏi ba câu: Ai viết? Tại sao? Người viết muốn gì? Mẹ cho Iris biết mẹ ở đâu và nhờ Iris giúp.

steps.en: Exam options use different words. *Please feed the cat* means 'Mum wants Iris to give the cat its dinner.'
steps.vi: Các lựa chọn trong bài thi dùng từ khác. *Please feed the cat* nghĩa là 'Mẹ muốn Iris cho mèo ăn tối.'

steps.en: Wrong options use words from the note but change the meaning, like 'Grandma is coming home at eight.'
steps.vi: Lựa chọn sai dùng từ trong ghi chú nhưng đổi nghĩa, ví dụ 'Bà sẽ về nhà lúc tám giờ.'

title.vi: Những câu thoại khớp với nhau

scenes.head: Two friends talking
scenes.html:
Viet: Do you want to come and watch the boat races on Saturday?
Holly: *I'd love to, but* I've got a bad cold.
Viet: *Oh no! I'm sorry.* Maybe next time.
Holly: *Thanks.* *How* are you getting there?
Viet: *By bus* with my dad.

steps.en: After a question, look for an answer. Holly answers, but she says no in a polite way.
steps.vi: Sau một câu hỏi, hãy tìm câu trả lời. Holly trả lời, nhưng từ chối một cách lịch sự.

steps.en: *Oh no! I'm sorry.* comes after bad news. A *How* question needs a way or a method: *By bus*.
steps.vi: *Oh no! I'm sorry.* đi sau một tin không vui. Câu hỏi *How* cần một cách thức: *By bus*.

steps.en: In Part 3, always check the line BEFORE and the line AFTER the gap.
steps.vi: Ở Phần 3, luôn kiểm tra câu NGAY TRƯỚC và câu NGAY SAU chỗ trống.

end.en: Great reading! You found what each notice and message really means.
end.vi: Đọc rất tốt! Em đã hiểu đúng ý nghĩa của từng thông báo và tin nhắn.

challenge.result: You spotted the rule words and chose lines that fit!

v.q: What does the sign say?
opts: Giving the ducks food is not allowed.
You can give the ducks a little bread.
The ducks are ill, so they can't eat.
whys: The sign says 'do not feed', so no bread at all, not even a little.
The ducks are not ill now. The sign says bread can make them ill.
v.hint: Find the words 'do not'. What must you NOT do?
v.worked: 'Please *do not feed* the ducks.' This means giving them food is not allowed.

stim.head: Sign at the lake
stim.html: Please do not feed the ducks. Bread makes them ill. Thank you!

v.q: Who must stay with an adult?
whys: A child of ten is not under 8, so this rule is not for them.
The rule is only for children under 8, not for every visitor.
v.hint: Find the age in the sign. Is each child older or younger than that?
v.worked: 'Children *under 8* must stay with an adult.' Six is under 8.

stim.head: Sign at the museum
stim.html: DINOSAUR ROOM: Children under 8 must stay with an adult. Please don't touch the bones.

v.q: What does Sami want Zoe to do?
opts: meet him a bit later than planned
walk to the park together with him
take the bus to the park gate
whys: Sami is walking alone. He wants Zoe to meet him at the gate.
The bus is late, so Sami isn't taking it.
v.hint: Find the word 'not'. What time did they plan, and what time is it now?
v.worked: 'Meet me at the gate at *ten past four, not four*.' That is a bit later.

stim.head: Text message
stim.html: Zoe, the bus is late, so I'm walking to the park. Meet me at the gate at ten past four, not four. Sami

v.q: Why has Alice written to Toby?
opts: to ask him to bring something
to invite him to a party at her house
to say she needs some cups
whys: The party is for the class, not at Alice's house.
Alice has already got the cups.
v.hint: Find the question in the email. What is Alice asking for?
v.worked: '*Could you bring some paper plates?*' Alice is asking Toby to bring something.

stim.head: Email
stim.html: Hi Toby, our class party is on Friday. Could you bring some paper plates? I've got the cups already. Thanks! Alice

v.q: Which option correctly completes the notice?
whys: 'Don't need to' means it is not necessary. This notice gives a rule: no food or drink.
'Could' is for polite questions or what is possible, not for rules.
v.hint: Read the next sentence. Is eating near the computers OK or not OK?
v.worked: Crumbs and water can damage the computers, so you *mustn't* eat or drink there.

stim.head: Notice in the library
stim.html: LIBRARY: You ________ eat or drink near the computers. Crumbs and water can damage them.

v.q: Which option correctly completes the message?
whys: 'Must you...?' sounds like a rule, not a polite request.
'Should' is for advice, not for asking a friend for help.
v.hint: An is asking a friend for help. Which word starts a polite question?
v.worked: '*Could* you lend me your blue pen, please?' is a polite request.

stim.head: Text message
stim.html: Hi Trang, ________ you lend me your blue pen, please? I left mine at home. An

v.q: Which option correctly completes the message?
whys: 'Was taking' talks about the past, but Sunday is in the future.
'Took' is the past, but Sunday is in the future.
v.hint: Is the trip in the past or the future? Who is doing it?
v.worked: A plan for Sunday: 'Dad *is taking* us to the zoo on Sunday.'

stim.head: Text message
stim.html: Hi Holly! Dad ________ us to the zoo on Sunday. Do you want to come? Iris

v.q:
Luca: 'I've lost my lunch box.'
Trang: '..........'
What is the best reply?
opts: Oh no! Shall I help you look?
whys: Luca isn't offering you anything to eat.
Losing something is bad news, not great news.
v.hint: Is Luca's news good or bad? What do friends say after bad news?
v.worked: After bad news, a friend is kind and helps: '*Oh no! Shall I help you look?*'

blurb.en: Learn the rule words, read short messages and choose replies that fit.
blurb.vi: Học từ chỉ quy định, đọc tin nhắn ngắn và chọn câu đáp phù hợp.

v.q: What does the sign say about phones?
opts: You can't use them during the film.
You must bring one to the film.
You can use them if you are quiet.
whys: The sign doesn't ask you to bring a phone. It asks you to switch it off.
'Mustn't' means not allowed, even if you are quiet.
v.hint: Find the word 'mustn't'. Does it mean 'not allowed' or 'not necessary'?
v.worked: 'You *mustn't* use it during the film.' Mustn't means it is not allowed.

stim.head: Sign at the cinema
stim.html: Please switch off your phone. You mustn't use it during the film. Enjoy the show!

v.q: What does the notice say about water?
opts: Students can get it at the tent.
Students must bring a bottle from home.
Students mustn't drink at the tent.
whys: 'Don't have to' means it is not necessary to bring water.
The free bottles are at the tent, so students can drink there.
v.hint: Find 'don't have to'. Is it a rule, or is it not necessary?
v.worked: 'You *don't have to* bring water: there are *free bottles at the tent*.'

stim.head: Notice in the classroom
stim.html: Tomorrow is Sports Day. You don't have to bring water: there are free bottles at the tent. You need to wear your PE kit.

v.q: Can you buy bread at 7 p.m.?
opts: No, the bakery is closed then.
Yes, but only the fresh bread.
Yes, because it's open every day.
whys: At 7 p.m. the bakery is closed, so you can't buy any bread.
It is open every day, but only until 6 p.m.
v.hint: Find the word 'until'. What happens after that time?
v.worked: 'Open every day *until 6 p.m.*' At 7 p.m. it is closed.

stim.head: Sign at the bakery
stim.html: Open every day until 6 p.m. Fresh bread comes out of the oven before 8 a.m.!

v.q: When must students give in their diaries?
whys: 'Before Friday' means Friday is already too late.
After the weekend is after Friday, so it is too late.
v.hint: Find the word 'before'. Which days are before it?
v.worked: 'Please hand in your reading diary *before Friday*.' Thursday is before Friday.

stim.head: Notice on the classroom door
stim.html: Please hand in your reading diary before Friday. Late diaries will not get a sticker.

v.q: What is free today?
opts: all the fruit and the juice
whys: 'Only' apples and bananas are free. You still pay for juice.
You still need to pay for the juice.
v.hint: Find the word 'only'. Then find what you need to pay for.
v.worked: 'FREE FRUIT TODAY: *apples and bananas only*.'

stim.head: Sign at the school canteen
stim.html: FREE FRUIT TODAY: apples and bananas only. You still need to pay for juice.

v.q: Who can use the big paints today?
whys: All students wash their brushes, but only Grade 4 can use the big paints.
Cleaning brushes is a rule for everyone. It doesn't decide who uses the big paints.
v.hint: Find 'all' and 'only'. Which rule is about the big paints?
v.worked: '*Only Grade 4* can use the big paints today.'

stim.head: Sign in the art room
stim.html: All students must wash their brushes after class. Only Grade 4 can use the big paints today.

title.vi: Tin nhắn ngắn: tại sao và cái gì?

v.q: Why has Viet written to Holly?
opts: to say he is ill and can't go out
to invite Holly to the cinema
to say his mum can't come tonight
whys: They already have a plan. Viet is saying he can't come.
Viet's mum isn't part of the plan. She only says Viet must stay in bed.
v.hint: Find 'I can't'. Then find the reason.
v.worked: '*I can't come*... *I've got a fever*.' Viet is ill, so he can't go out.

stim.head: Text message
stim.html: Hi Holly, I can't come to the cinema tonight. I've got a fever and Mum says I must stay in bed. Sorry! Viet

v.q: Why has Alice written the note?
opts: to explain where Toby's ball is
to ask Toby to play in the park
to say Toby's football is flat
whys: Alice doesn't invite Toby. She tells him what she did.
It's Alice's ball that is flat, not Toby's.
v.hint: Whose ball is flat? Whose ball is at the park?
v.worked: 'I've *taken your football to the park* because *mine* is flat.'

stim.head: Sticky note
stim.html: Toby, I've taken your football to the park because mine is flat. I'll give it back after dinner! Alice

v.q: What does Iris want Trang to do?
opts: look after the plant next week
move the plant to the window
buy a new plant for the class
whys: The plant is already on the window. Trang doesn't need to move it.
Iris doesn't ask for a new plant. She asks Trang to water this one.
v.hint: Find the question that starts with 'Could you...?'.
v.worked: '*Could you water it* for me?' while Iris is away next week.

stim.head: Email
stim.html: Dear Trang, our class plant needs water every day. I'm away next week. Could you water it for me? It's on the window by the door. Thanks, Iris

v.q: What does Dad want Luca to do?
opts: finish work at half past five
whys: Dad is bringing the fish home, not Luca.
Dad is the one at work. Luca has to start the rice at half past five.
v.hint: Find 'Can you...?'. What does Dad ask Luca to do?
v.worked: '*Can you start cooking the rice* at half past five?' The rice is part of dinner.

stim.head: Phone message
stim.html: Luca, it's Dad. I'm still at work. Can you start cooking the rice at half past five? I'll bring some fish home.

v.q: How does Sami feel?
whys: Sami got 10 out of 10, so he isn't worried.
He practised every evening and wants to celebrate, so he isn't bored.
v.hint: Look at his score and the last sentence. Is he happy or unhappy?
v.worked: 'I got *10 out of 10*!' and '*Let's celebrate*!' show he is proud.

stim.head: Text message
stim.html: Zoe, I got 10 out of 10 in the spelling test! I practised every evening with Grandpa. Let's celebrate with ice cream! Sami

v.q: What can An eat now?
opts: the cake that is on the table
whys: The cake is for Grandpa's birthday tonight, so An mustn't eat it.
Mum says there are biscuits in the cupboard, so An can eat something.
v.hint: Find what An mustn't eat. Then find what Mum offers instead.
v.worked: 'There are *biscuits in the cupboard*.' The cake is for Grandpa.

stim.head: Note on the kitchen table
stim.html: An, please don't eat the cake on the table. It's for Grandpa's birthday tonight! There are biscuits in the cupboard. Mum

v.q: Holly asks: 'How are we getting to the museum?' What is the best reply?
opts: Yes, I really want to go.
whys: 'How' asks about the way you travel, not the time.
'How...?' is not a yes / no question.
v.hint: Look at the question word. What does 'How' ask about here?
v.worked: '*How* are we getting there?' asks about travel, so '*By bus*' answers it.

v.q: Viet asks: 'Where shall we meet?' What is the best reply?
whys: 'On Saturday morning' tells you when, not where.
'With my brother' tells you who, not where.
v.hint: 'Where' asks about a place. Find a place.
v.worked: '*Where* shall we meet?' '*Outside the library*.' That is a place.

v.q:
Trang: 'I can't come to the party. I've got a stomach ache.'
Toby: '..........'
What can Toby say?
opts: Oh dear! I hope you feel better soon.
Great! See you at the party on Saturday, then.
Yes, please. I'd love a piece.
whys: Trang can't come, so 'See you at the party' doesn't fit.
Nobody is offering Toby any food.
v.hint: Is Trang's news good or bad? What do we say after bad news?
v.worked: A stomach ache is bad news, so Toby says '*Oh dear! I hope you feel better soon*.'

v.q: Iris: 'My grandpa is in hospital.' What is the best reply?
whys: Being in hospital is not fun. This reply is for good news.
'Me too, thanks' doesn't answer sad news about her grandpa.
v.hint: Is the news happy or sad?
v.worked: Sad news needs a kind reply: '*I'm sorry to hear that*.'

v.q:
Luca: 'Why don't we make a card for our teacher?'
Zoe: '..........'
opts: Good idea! I've got some coloured paper.
Because she's always very kind to all of us.
whys: 'Why don't we...?' is a suggestion, not a real 'why' question.
Luca is talking about the future, not something in the past.
v.hint: Is Luca asking for a reason, or giving an idea?
v.worked: '*Why don't we*...?' is a suggestion, so Zoe answers '*Good idea!*'

v.q:
An: 'The shop has no milk.'
Sami: '..........'
An: 'Good idea. Let's go there.'
What fits the gap?
opts: I don't like milk very much.
whys: An says 'Let's go there', so Sami must name a place.
'We bought some yesterday' isn't an idea, and it doesn't name a place.
v.hint: Read the line AFTER the gap. What does 'there' need?
v.worked: '*The market* sells milk too.' 'Good idea. Let's go *there*.'

blurb.en: Practise Reading Part 2 (short texts) and Part 3 (complete the conversation).
blurb.vi: Luyện Phần 2 của bài Đọc (văn bản ngắn) và Phần 3 (hoàn thành đoạn hội thoại).

title.vi: Phần 2: thông báo và biển báo

v.q: What does it say?
opts: A nine-year-old needs an adult in the big pool.
All children must swim in the small pool.
Everyone must have a shower after they finish swimming.
whys: Children can use the small pool, but they don't have to.
The notice says shower BEFORE you swim, not after.
v.hint: Find the age in the notice. Then find 'before'.
v.worked: 'Children *under 10 must swim with an adult* in the big pool.' Nine is under 10.

stim.head: Notice at the swimming pool
stim.html: Children under 10 must swim with an adult in the big pool. The small pool is open to everyone. Please shower before you swim.

v.q: What does it say?
opts: Put on repellent before PE outside.
Leave water in pots for the plants.
There is no PE outside this month.
whys: The notice says do NOT leave water standing in pots.
Outdoor PE still happens. You use repellent before it.
v.hint: Find 'do not'. Then find what to do before outdoor PE.
v.worked: 'Please *use repellent before outdoor PE*.' Repellent stops mosquito bites.

stim.head: Notice at the school office
stim.html: Mosquitoes are bad this month. Please use repellent before outdoor PE. Do not leave water standing in pots or bottles in the garden.

v.q: What does it say?
opts: The photos will be taken later than planned.
Students should wear PE kit on Wednesday.
Photo day is still on Monday this week.
whys: The notice says wear school uniform, NOT PE kit.
Photo day has moved from Monday to Wednesday.
v.hint: Find the word 'moved'. Is the new day earlier or later?
v.worked: 'Photo day has *moved from Monday to Wednesday*.' Wednesday is later.

stim.head: Notice on the classroom door
stim.html: School photo day has moved from Monday to Wednesday. Please wear your school uniform, not your PE kit. Each photo costs £5.

v.q: What does it say?
opts: You can't buy a hot meal here today.
The café is closed until Saturday.
Cakes are sold on Saturday only.
whys: The café is open today. Only the kitchen is closed.
Cakes are on sale today too.
v.hint: What is closed: the café or the kitchen? What can you still buy?
v.worked: 'Our *kitchen is closed* today... *Hot food is back on Saturday*.' So no hot meals today.

stim.head: Notice at the café
stim.html: Our kitchen is closed today. We are selling drinks and cakes only. Hot food is back on Saturday. Sorry! The café team

v.q: What should parents who drive do in the morning?
opts: send their children on the school bus
whys: The notice doesn't ask parents to use the buses. It tells them where to park.
7.30 is between 7.15 and 7.45, so parents mustn't park outside the gate then.
v.hint: Find 'do not'. Then find where parents CAN park.
v.worked: '*You can park in Green Street*.' That is another street.

stim.head: Notice at the school gate
stim.html: Parents, please do not park outside the gate between 7.15 and 7.45 a.m. The school buses need this space. You can park in Green Street.

v.q: What does it say?
opts: Adults can get in free on Sundays.
Taking photos is not allowed here.
whys: Adults pay £4. Only children are free on Sundays.
Photos are allowed. You just mustn't use a flash.
v.hint: Who gets free entry, and when?
v.worked: '*Free entry for children on Sundays*.' Free means they don't pay.

stim.head: Sign at the history museum
stim.html: Free entry for children on Sundays. Adults pay £4. Photos are allowed, but please don't use a flash. Open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.

v.q: Which option correctly completes the notice?
whys: 'Don't need to' means it is not necessary. Here touching is not allowed.
'Would' is for polite questions, not for rules.
v.hint: Read the reason in the next sentence. Is touching OK or not OK?
v.worked: We are measuring the plants, so you *mustn't* touch them.

stim.head: Notice in the science room
stim.html: SCIENCE ROOM: You ________ touch the plants on the window. We are measuring how fast they grow. Thank you, Class 4A.

v.q: Which option correctly completes the notice?
whys: 'Mustn't' means it is not allowed, but the notice only says the farm gives you lunch.
'Could' doesn't say if something is necessary or not.
v.hint: Read the first part: the farm gives everyone lunch. So is bringing food necessary?
v.worked: 'The farm gives everyone lunch, *so* you *don't need to* bring food.'

stim.head: Notice about the farm trip
stim.html: FARM TRIP: The farm gives everyone lunch, so you ________ bring food. Please bring a water bottle and a sun hat.

v.q: Which option correctly completes the message?
whys: 'Must you...?' sounds like a rule, not a friendly request.
'Should' is for advice. Trang is asking a friend for help.
v.hint: Trang is asking for help. Which word starts a polite question?
v.worked: '*Could* you help me with my maths homework?' is a polite request.

stim.head: Text message
stim.html: Hi Zoe, ________ you help me with my maths homework after school? I don't understand the fractions at all. Thanks! Trang

v.q: Which option correctly completes the note?
whys: 'Must you...?' is not polite. It sounds like a rule.
'Should' gives advice. Iris and Mum are asking for help.
v.hint: They need help and say 'please'. Which word starts a polite request?
v.worked: '*Would* you feed our fish, please?' is a polite request.

stim.head: Note to a neighbour
stim.html: Hello! We are going on holiday tomorrow. ________ you feed our fish, please? The food is in a blue box by the door. Thank you! Iris and Mum

v.q: Which option correctly completes the message?
whys: 'Arrived' is the past, but Friday is in the future: there is a welcome dinner on Saturday.
After 'My cousin' we need 'is arriving', not 'arrive'.
v.hint: Is the cousin's visit in the past or the future? Look at the days.
v.worked: A plan for Friday: 'My cousin *is arriving* from Australia on Friday.'

stim.head: Text message
stim.html: Hi Sami! My cousin ________ from Australia on Friday. Can you come to our welcome dinner on Saturday evening? We're having pizza! Holly

v.q: Which option correctly completes the email?
whys: 'Had' is the past, but 'next Monday' is in the future.
After 'we' we need 'are having', not 'has'.
v.hint: Find the time words 'next Monday'. Who is the subject?
v.worked: A plan: 'We *are having* a cake sale... *next Monday*.'

stim.head: Email
stim.html: Dear Luca, we ________ a cake sale for the children's hospital next Monday. Can you make some biscuits? Thanks, Zoe

title.vi: Phần 3: hoàn thành đoạn hội thoại

v.q: Choose the best answer for gap (1).
v.hint: Read the line AFTER the gap. What is Sami saying 'Don't worry' about?
v.worked: 'Shall we visit her?' 'Good idea, but we should *ask her mum first*.' 'Don't worry. *I phoned her mum*.' (E)

stim.head: Conversation: Sami and Iris
stim.html:
Sami: Hi Iris! Is Trang at school today?
Iris: (0) C
Sami: Oh no! Shall we visit her on Saturday?
Iris: (1) ________
Sami: Don't worry. I phoned her mum this morning, and she said yes.
Iris: (2) ________
Sami: After lunch, at about two. Trang sleeps a lot in the morning.
Iris: (3) ________
Sami: We can walk. Her flat is only ten minutes from the park.
Iris: (4) ________
Sami: Yes! Some oranges. She loves them, and they've got lots of vitamins.
Iris: (5) ________
Sami: Lovely. See you at the park gate at two, then.
bank: Great! What time shall we go?

items.en: *must* and *need to* = it is necessary. *mustn't* = it is not allowed. *don't have to* / *don't need to* = it is not necessary. *should* = it is a good idea.
items.vi: *must* và *need to* = cần thiết, bắt buộc. *mustn't* = không được phép. *don't have to* / *don't need to* = không cần thiết. *should* = nên làm.
example: You *don't need to* bring paper: we have lots.

items.en: A polite question to ask for help starts with *Could you...?* or *Would you...?*. Invitations often start with *Would you like...?*.
items.vi: Câu hỏi lịch sự để nhờ giúp đỡ bắt đầu bằng *Could you...?* hoặc *Would you...?*. Lời mời thường bắt đầu bằng *Would you like...?*.
example: *Would* you like to come to my party?

items.en: For a plan in the future, use *am / is / are + -ing* with a future time word (tomorrow, on Sunday, next week).
items.vi: Để nói về kế hoạch trong tương lai, dùng *am / is / are + -ing* với từ chỉ thời gian tương lai (tomorrow, on Sunday, next week).
example: Dad *is taking* us to the zoo *on Sunday*.
We *are having* a cake sale *next Monday*.

items.en: Small words change the meaning a lot: *before*, *after*, *until*, *only*, *all*, *some*.
items.vi: Những từ nhỏ làm thay đổi nghĩa rất nhiều: *before*, *after*, *until*, *only*, *all*, *some*.
example: The big slide is for Grade 4 *only*.

items.en: The right option says the same idea in different words (a *paraphrase*). Wrong options use words from the text but change the meaning.
items.vi: Lựa chọn đúng nói cùng một ý bằng từ khác (*diễn đạt lại*). Lựa chọn sai dùng từ trong bài nhưng đổi nghĩa.
example: Right option: '*You can't eat* in the library.'

items.en: In a conversation, check the line *before* AND the line *after* the gap. A question needs an answer; bad news needs a kind reply; 'Good idea!' follows a suggestion.
items.vi: Trong hội thoại, kiểm tra câu *trước* VÀ câu *sau* chỗ trống. Câu hỏi cần câu trả lời; tin không vui cần câu đáp tử tế; 'Good idea!' đi sau một lời gợi ý.
example: A: *How* are we getting there? B: *By bus*.
A: I've got a cold. B: *Oh dear! I hope you feel better*.

check.sentence: You {don't need to|mustn't|should} bring a pen: there are pens on every desk.
My aunt {is visiting|visited|visit} us next weekend.
'Open until 4 p.m.' means that at 5 p.m. it is {closed|open|busy}.
A: I've lost my bag. B: {Oh no! Can I help?|Great! Well done.|Yes, I'd love to.}
